matchups.analysis: Both teams are sitting at 0.0 with fully loaded rosters still to play, but ESPN's already handing this to Veton at 57% with a projected 9.3-point gap (78.9 to 69.6), which is basically saying Rob's got the harder path even though both sides have nine guys left on the field. Rob's got the better individual talent with CMC and Garrett Wilson, but Veton stacked the late window with Ja'Marr Chase and Josh Jacobs in what could turn into a blowout, while Rob's relying on his entire bench showing up and overperforming at the same time—ESPN's math says that happens 43% of the time and honestly that might be generous. Neither guy made a benching blunder, so this is pure execution, but the projection favors Veton's roster construction and depth enough that you should already be nervous if you're banking on Rob catching a late-game miracle.

Faton's at 45% and Ben's at 55%, ESPN projecting a 7-point gap that'll come down to execution—both lineups are fully loaded so this absolutely stays competitive until the late slots kick off. The issue is Ben's got the cleaner roster construction with Kelce and Justin Jefferson still pending; Faton needs Drake London, D'Andre Swift, and Rome Odunze to all hit their floors while Ben's basically just waiting for his studs to show up and be studs. ESPN's saying Ben wins this 55% of the time, but if Faton's receivers actually catch passes and his RBs get fed, this one stays tight—just don't expect the comeback when you're asking five different guys to deliver simultaneously while Ben's got two all-world names waiting in the wings.

Nori's walking out of here at 84% with ESPN projecting a 57.6-point gap (112.7 to 55.1), and that's before half these lineups even check in—Ilir's got nine guys left to play and it still doesn't matter because Nori's got Jahmyr Gibbs, Breece Hall, Christian Watson, and Brock Bowers all pending, which is basically just asking if Ilir can overcome an entire elite receiving corps while his own guys deliver ceiling games across the board. The math is suffocating: Gibbs and Hall are both projected north of 15 points each, Watson's getting 12+, and Bowers is sitting at 10—that's 50+ points from four players before you even count Javonte Williams or Jared Goff, and Ilir's banking on C.J. Stroud, Bijan Robinson, and George Pickens all going absolutely nuclear to even make this competitive. Nori didn't need a perfect storm; he just needed a competent roster, and that's exactly what he's sitting on—Ilir's the one staring at needing his entire bench to explode while hoping Nori's studs somehow underperform their projections by 10+ points each, which ESPN's basically saying won't happen 84% of the time.

ESPN's got Arben walking out of here at 55% with a 9.3-point projected edge (113.7 to 104.4), but Jetmir's still got nine starters left to run out so this isn't sealed yet—Kenneth Walker, Caleb Williams, and Tetairoa McMillan are exactly the kind of names that can chip away at a single-digit deficit if the slate breaks right. The problem is Arben's bench is just as loaded: Jonathan Taylor, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and Jaylen Warren are all still pending, which means this thing could easily swing into comfortable territory for either guy depending on whose studs actually deliver their floor. Both rosters are clean with no meaningful benching disasters, so this one's genuinely coming down to execution and whether the projected gap holds up once everyone's locked in—Arben's got the slight edge because his lineup feels marginally more consistent top-to-bottom, but Jetmir's absolutely still alive if his later slots go off. This stays competitive until the final whistle.

Rilind's sitting at 42% and ESPN's got him projecting to 88.4, which sounds hopeful until you remember Flamur's already locked in at 100.9 with CeeDee Lamb, Saquon Barkley, and Tee Higgins all still waiting to punch their tickets. The gap's already 12.5 points and Flamur's got three elite-tier weapons left while Rilind's banking on Amon-Ra, Ashton Jeanty, and Matthew Stafford all hitting their ceiling simultaneously—ESPN's basically saying that happens less than half the time, and honestly they're probably being nice about it. Neither guy made a trainwreck benching decision, so this one comes down to pure roster construction, and Flamur just straight-up built better with his late-round stack while Rilind's got more question marks in his remaining lineup. This one's getting away from you unless Jeanty decides to have the game of his life.

Both teams are sitting at 0.0 with completely full lineups still to play, which means this is legitimately a toss-up on paper—ESPN's got Adam favored at 51% with a 2.3-point projected edge (110.4 to 108.1), but neither one of you has actually locked anything in yet. Adam's got the slightly cleaner roster top-to-bottom with A.J. Brown and Puka Nacua still pending while Rinor's banking on Derrick Henry and DK Metcalf actually showing up, and that's usually where these coin flips get decided—whose studs remember they're studs when the games matter. Neither guy made any bone-headed benching decisions, so this comes down to pure execution and who gets the production they're projected for, which is basically asking whose guys decide to be competent on Sunday. The math says Adam edges this out if both teams get their projected floors, but you're one boom performance away from watching this flip entirely—this stays tight until the last kickoff wraps up.
